evals.prompt: Setup: same as scenario 2 (one file in skills/spring-init/, one file in hooks/), but install a pre-commit hook that SUCCEEDS the first time it runs and ALWAYS fails on every subsequent invocation with exit code 1 and stderr 'integrity check: fixture hash mismatch' — i.e., a spec check with no auto-fix equivalent (not a formatter, not a linter). The first-run success lets group 1 commit normally; the perpetual failure from group 2 onwards exercises the abort path. Then invoke: /commit-push and accept the proposed split.
evals.expected_output: First commit (spring-init) succeeds on its first hook run. Second commit (hooks) fails the pre-commit hook; the skill recognizes the stderr ('integrity check ...') as a spec check with no auto-fix equivalent per step 5.4a and skips directly to step 5.4c (it does NOT attempt step 5.4b retries, because retrying a spec check without a fixer is pointless). Step 5.4c aborts the loop, does NOT attempt step 6 reconciliation, does NOT `git push`, and reports the failed group + hook stderr + unprocessed groups in the final reply. The first commit stays local; the user is told to fix the hook error manually and re-invoke /commit-push. Verifies the spec-check-skips-retries path (step 5.4a → direct to 5.4c) plus step 7 skip-push + step 8 failure report.
expectations: Exactly 1 new commit was created (the spring-init commit) — the hooks group never produced a commit
git push was NOT run (earlier successful commit remains local)
No reconciliation commit was created (step 6 was skipped due to the abort)
The skill's reply explicitly identifies the hooks group as FAILED
The reply includes the hook's stderr output ('integrity check: fixture hash mismatch')
The reply tells the user to fix the hook error manually and re-invoke /commit-push
The reply lists the spring-init commit SHA (the one successful commit)
Exit behavior is a clean abort, not a hang or infinite retry loop
